name: a shallow rain puddle lying on the ground, reflecting a pale sky band, with a soft damp earth halo and only a faint low bank shadow along its far edge
label: wasteland_ruins/puddle

surfaces.part: puddle water surface (teal ellipse with pale sky reflection streaks)
damp earth halo and faint dark bank shadow around the puddle's far edge

answer.evidence: The 64x48 canvas is a full-bleed earth ground texture with a small elliptical puddle in the middle, about rows 20-28 and roughly 12 px wide. The puddle's width grows and then shrinks again, so it reads as an ellipse seen from above. It has no vertical front face (0 rows), no side face and no front-edge line. It is a flat decal lying on the ground, which matches the flat kind and reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown soil patch with a small blue puddle in the centre. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile (reference grass 3, paving 7), 1% near-flat coverage, 0% neutral dark edge pixels. So it is not flat and has no black sticker outline. The soil carries speckle and grain in several browns, and the damp halo is soft. Weaknesses: the puddle is tiny, only about 2 tones (a pale reflection band on a mid blue) with no bank shading or clear halo ramp. Only 11 distinct colours overall, so the soil ramp is about 4 steps against the references' 5-6. The soil grain is fairly uniform and sparse, with fewer clumps and variation than the Beodeul grass and paving. It is close to the reference but a bit shallower in shading depth, and the puddle focal element is under-built. When in doubt, fail.
